trust_decision.summary: The `fonts` option is base64-JSON decoded from the unauthenticated image URL and each entry's `path` becomes `font.src`, which the platform font-asset binding hands to a raw same-origin URL join + fetch with no host classification; the decision that a font path may be fetched must be made inside the binding (before the fetch) and, for the same-origin case, inside the shared SSRF guard.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names `fonts[].path`; `loadDefinedFonts` is the only function that turns an attacker-supplied `fonts[]` entry into a FontConfig and calls the virtual font-asset `resolve`, so it is the first place an engineer who read only the summary will look.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second font source field on the same FontConfig (a src/url alias, or a localPath-only entry) that reaches the fetch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: FontConfig already carries both src and localPath and loadDefinedFonts sets both from the single path, so a maintainer adding a separate field is a one-line change that bypasses a gate keyed on `path`.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another base64-JSON option that carries URLs (like takumi.images / _query) reaching a fetch
